title: Polynomial-time closure under unary addition
statement: Let $f,g$ map binary strings to natural numbers. If the unary words consisting of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ copies of $1$ are each polynomial-time computable, then the unary word consisting of $f(x)+g(x)$ copies of $1$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $f,g$ map binary strings to natural numbers
The unary word for $f(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
The unary word for $g(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If two unary values are polynomial-time computable, then the unary word of their sum is polynomial-time computable by literal concatenation.
